copy.hero_headline: Your dock becomes a station on a connected harbor network.
copy.hero_sub: Your dock becomes a station on a connected water network. Boston already proves the harbor commute — the MBTA ferry carried nearly 1.5 million riders last year and now runs a year-round inner-harbor loop. Navier adds a premium employer-sponsored tier on top: 30-seat electric hydrofoils linking Salem, Hingham, Hull, Quincy Marina Bay, downtown, and the Seaport — including year-round marina-grade stations the public system doesn't serve today.
copy.hero_note: Non-binding letter of intent · first service no earlier than end-2027 · premium tier alongside MBTA, not a replacement
copy.hero_cta_network: Find a route to my office
copy.problem_title: The harbor is the spare lane.
copy.problem_lead: Boston has the 4th-worst traffic congestion in the US (~$1,400 lost per driver per year), and I-93 south of downtown is the 2nd-most-congested road in the country. Meanwhile the harbor commute is already proven: the MBTA ferry is the system's best-performing mode, Hingham and Hull commuters ride 18–19 round trips a day, and when the Sumner Tunnel closed, the state itself pointed the North Shore to the water. Every launch station is a working ferry landing or marina today — no new construction on day one.

problem_chips.label: MBTA ferry riders in 2025 — proof the water works
Inner harbor: displacement speed for every vessel
Employer seats + marina stations MBTA does not serve

copy.precedent: The MBTA and Massport run one of the best public ferry systems in America — we're building alongside it, not against it. Navier adds guaranteed employer seats where the public boats are full or don't go: a Seaport leg for South Shore riders, year-round service at Marina Bay, and a Salem station the network has never had.
copy.stripe_lesson: First employer water commute on San Francisco Bay. Boston already has the best ferry OTP on the T — we add a premium employer tier.
copy.price_anchor: Program band seat-month pricing — not a Boston quote; market-specific pricing TBD
copy.launch_trigger: A line advances when about 60–80 seats are committed on that corridor.
copy.proof_title: Boston already funds the water commute.
copy.proof_lead: The MBTA and Massport run one of the best public ferry systems in America — we're building alongside it, not against it. Navier adds guaranteed employer seats where the public boats are full or don't go: a Seaport leg for South Shore riders, year-round service at Marina Bay, and a Salem station the network has never had.
copy.proof_worked_body: MBTA ferry ~1.5M riders (2025); F10 year-round inner-harbor loop; Salem Ferry already sells commuter-rate rush-hour tickets.
copy.proof_fixed_body: First employer water commute on SF Bay — premium tier alongside the proven system.
copy.proof_ask_body: Non-binding LOI — seats or line anchor — so we sequence on real demand.
copy.network_lead: Five clear corridors — not nine overlapping feeders. North Shore and South Shore spines into the downtown hubs; Quincy across Dorchester Bay; Inner Harbor (no-wake) for Charlestown / East Boston / Winthrop; Riverside for Encore / Lovejoy. Transfer at Long Wharf, Rowes Wharf, or Fan Pier. All water times are indicative; inner-harbor and Riverside legs are no-wake.
copy.network_footnote: Gold rings mark transfer hubs (Long Wharf, Rowes Wharf, Fan Pier). MECE lines: North Shore · South Shore · Quincy · Inner Harbor · Riverside. Lynn, Weymouth, and Scituate sit on the shore spines — not orphan expresses. Alongside the MBTA ferry — premium employer tier, not a replacement. No Logan stop.
copy.map_detail_empty: Pick two terminals in Find my ride — or select a line or stop.
copy.calc_lead_html: Optional planning math. Seat pricing uses the global program band, not a Boston quote. Inner-harbor times are no-wake / indicative.
copy.loi_cta: Register interest with a non-binding letter of intent. It costs nothing and reserves nothing — it tells us which corridors to launch first.
copy.footer_note: Letters of intent are non-binding. Service launch not before end-2027. Alongside the MBTA ferry — not a replacement.
copy.office_lead: Sit on Long Wharf, Rowes Wharf, or Fan Pier — or any stop that feeds one — and riders transfer to you.
copy.office_insight: Example: an LOI at Fan Pier still serves Salem, Hingham, and Marina Bay riders who transfer downtown.
copy.why_lead: The harbor is the spare lane. Outer legs can foil; inner harbor is no-wake for everyone.
